dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Quando as frações têm denominadores diferentes, o que acontece com o tamanho de cada 'pedaço' quando dividimos o mesmo inteiro em mais ou menos partes?
Tente marcar o ponto 5/6 na primeira reta e o ponto 4/5 na segunda. Depois de marcar, observe qual ponto está mais próximo do número 1.
Dica: Tente encontrar um denominador comum para 6 e 5, ou simplesmente veja qual fração está mais perto do final da reta (o número 1).
Pense assim: 5/6 é apenas 1/6 para chegar a um inteiro. 4/5 é 1/5 para chegar a um inteiro. Qual 'pedaço' é menor: 1/6 ou 1/5? Se o pedaço que falta é menor, a fração é maior!

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Daryl's paper chain" e "Rashad's paper chain"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Daryl built the longer paper chain."; "Rashad built the longer paper chain."; "Both built the same length of paper chain."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

seletor com as alternativas de comparação; o aluno escolhe uma delas

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number line?

The denominator is the number below the fraction bar in Daryl's measurement.

Select the statement naming the person whose marked point is farther right on the number line.

Rashad's  paper chain is 4/5 feet long.
Who built a longer piece of paper chain?

Look at the bottom number in Daryl's fraction and use it as the number of equal intervals.
The denominator is the number below the fraction bar in Daryl's measurement.
Enter the denominator of Daryl's fraction in the field and confirm that many equal intervals.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas (traços) em vez dos intervalos, resultando em um erro de contagem 'off-by-one'.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted the marks instead of the intervals. To divide Daryl's line into 6 equal parts, count the spaces between the marks.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ignora a necessidade de dividir a reta em partes fracionárias e trata a reta como unidade única.
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the whole number line as one part. The denominator tells us to divide Daryl's line into equal fractional parts.

nodes.description: Mark Daryl's fraction on the first number line.
nodes.instruction: Mark Daryl's fraction on the first number line.

hints.message: Which number tells how many equal parts to count from zero?
Use the numerator to count intervals from 0 after the line has been divided by the denominator.
Start at 0 and move toward 1, counting the intervals named by the top number of Daryl's fraction.
Click the point reached after counting five intervals out of the six equal intervals.

nodes.description: Divide Rashad's number line into equal parts for his fraction.
nodes.instruction: Divide Rashad's number line into equal parts for his fraction.

hints.message: What does the denominator represent in Rashad's fraction?
Find the bottom number in Rashad's fraction and use it to set the number of equal intervals.
Rashad's denominator is the number below the fraction bar.
Enter Rashad's denominator and confirm that many equal intervals on the second number line.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas (traços) em vez dos intervalos, resultando em um erro de contagem 'off-by-one'.
misconceptions.feedback: You counted four marks instead of five intervals. Count the spaces that divide Rashad's number line.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ignora a necessidade de dividir a reta em partes fracionárias e trata a reta como unidade única.
misconceptions.feedback: You used one whole interval instead of fractional intervals. Rashad's denominator determines the number of equal parts.

nodes.description: Mark Rashad's fraction on the second number line.
nodes.instruction: Mark Rashad's fraction on the second number line.

hints.message: Which part of a fraction tells how many intervals to count?
Start at 0 and count intervals using the numerator after the denominator has set the equal parts.
Count four intervals toward 1 on Rashad's number line.
Click the point reached after four of the five equal intervals.

acceptableVariations: Daryl built the longer paper chain.

options.feedback: Good effort checking the distance to 1, but the denominator changes the size of each part. Compare the positions of 5/6 and 4/5.

options.value: Both built the same length of paper chain.

options.feedback: The fractions are not equal. Even if both are one part away from 1, their denominators make the parts different sizes.

hints.message: On number lines with the same endpoints, which point represents the greater length?
Compare the locations of the two marked points between 0 and 1.
Look for the point that is farther to the right, not just the fraction with the larger numerator.
Select the statement naming the person whose marked point is farther right on the number line.

nodes.description: Finish the problem after confirming the comparison.

hints.message: Are both fractions located between 0 and 1 on their number lines?
Use the marked positions to confirm which fraction is greater before completing the problem.
Check that Daryl's point is farther right and that both points remain below 1.
After confirming the comparison, activate the Done button to submit the completed problem.
